To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
D7 proteins, a family of secreted proteins in mosquito salivary glands that are expressed during blood feeding, can inhibit dengue virus infection.
Ae. aeygpti D7 saliva proteins inhibit DENV infection through direct binding to virions.
D7 protein inhibits DENV infection in a dose-dependent manner in vitro and in a mouse model, and D7 protein binds to DENV virions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of mosquito saliva in arbovirus pathogenesis and transmission, which may provide new insights into the mechanisms of arbovirus infection and transmission, and new targets for arbovirus control.
the identification of novel arbovirus antagonists from arthropod vectors.
the role of saliva in DENV transmission and provides a novel mechanism by which saliva proteins inhibit virus transmission
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
D7 proteins can bind to the DENV virion and inhibit infection.
Ae. aeygpti D7 proteins inhibit DENV infection through direct interaction with virion and/or viral envelope protein, and this interaction may be mediated through a specific binding motif.
D7 protein is an inhibitor of DENV infection and this protein may play a role in the inhibition of DENV transmission to vertebrates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a novel role for a salivary protein, D7 protein in Ae. aegpyti, which inhibits transmission of DENV by binding to virions.
we show that Ae. aepgtyi saliva contains proteins that inhibit dengue virus transmission to vertebrates.
Ae. aegispti saliva contains both inhibitory and enhancing factors for DENV infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
D7 proteins, and possibly other saliva proteins, inhibit dengue virus infection in vitro and vivo.
Ae. aeygpti D7 saliva protein is a novel inhibitor of DENV infection.
the Ae. aegpyti salivary gland proteins have diverse roles in the transmission process and that some of these proteins can directly interact with virus particles to modulate infection.
